messages.content: Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle

reasoning:
The user wants an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle. Let me create a nice, detailed SVG illustration.

Let me think about composition: a bicycle with two wheels, frame, handlebars, seat, pedals. A pelican sitting on the seat, with a big beak/pouch, wings gripping handlebars, legs on pedals.

Let me design carefully with coordinates. Canvas 800x600.

Ground line at y=500.

Wheels: rear wheel center (250, 420) radius 80; front wheel center (560, 420) radius 80. So wheels touch ground at y=500. Good.

Frame: classic diamond frame. Bottom bracket at (390, 420). Seat tube from bottom bracket up-back to seat at (330, 320). Top tube from (330,320) area to head tube top (500, 330). Down tube from bottom bracket (390,420) to head tube bottom (505, 375). Chain stays from bottom bracket (390,420) to rear hub (250,420). Seat stays from seat cluster (330,320) to rear hub (250,420). Fork: head tube from (500,330) to (505,375), then fork blades down to front hub (560,420). Handlebars at (500,320) going up and curving.

Crank: crank arm from bottom bracket to pedal. Pedal at (430, 470) forward-down, and other pedal at (350, 370) back-up. Pelican feet on pedals.

Pelican: sitting on seat around (330, 300). Body ellipse centered (340, 270) rx 70 ry 55. Neck going up-right to head at (450, 200). Beak long pointing right-down with pouch. Wing over body reaching down to handlebars at (505, 315).

Hmm, pelican riding bicycle — head should be near handlebars, forward. Let's place head at (470, 190), beak extending right to (560, 240) with pouch below.

Actually pelicans have huge beak with a pouch. Let's draw beak as a long triangle-ish shape from head to tip at (575, 215), and pouch as a curved bag hanging beneath.

Wing: draw a wing shape with feather strokes, and an arm/wing reaching to handlebar grip.

Let me also add a scarf/hat? Keep it charming. Maybe add a small helmet? Could be cute. I'll add a little aviator cap or just leave. Maybe a scarf flying behind — nice detail.

Colors: pelican body white/cream (#f6efe3), beak orange-yellow (#e8a13c / #f2b64e), pouch lighter (#f7c784), wing grey (#c9b79b), eye dark, legs orange-yellow, feet dark. Bicycle: teal/red frame (#d1495b or #2f6f6a). Let's use frame color #e0653f? Let me choose a warm palette: sky gradient background light blue, ground pale.

Let me write the SVG carefully.

Structure:
- defs: gradients (sky, wheel rim), maybe a subtle shadow.
- background rect with sky gradient, sun, clouds.
- ground ellipse/road.
- bicycle (behind pelican): wheels with spokes, tires, frame lines, chain, crank, pedals, seat, handlebar.
- pelican: legs (behind), body, wing, neck, head, beak, eye, crest feather.
- motion lines / dust.

I'll make sure z-order works: draw bike frame, then pelican legs on pedals, then pelican body, wing, head. Actually pedal crank should be in front of feet? Feet on pedals — draw pedal then foot.

Order: wheels, frame, chain, seat, handlebar, pelican body+wing+head, then legs and feet? Legs come from body down to pedal, so draw legs after body (they attach at body lower area). Fine: draw legs first then body? Legs emerge from body underside; drawing legs after body is fine since they're in front. But then pedal under foot: draw pedal/crank before legs. Let's do: bike (incl. crank+pedals), then pelican legs+feet, then body, wing, neck, head, beak. Hmm body drawn after legs would cover leg tops — that's fine, legs come out from under body. But body drawn later would cover leg tops which is desired.

Wait, the seat should be under the pelican body; body drawn after seat covers it. Good.

Spokes: I'll generate via a group with rotated lines using transform rotate around hub center.

Let me write spokes: for hub at (cx,cy), lines from cx-74 to cx+74 horizontally? Simpler: draw a group of 8 lines rotated by 0..135 degrees: `<g transform="translate(cx,cy)"> <line x1="-74" y1="0" x2="74" y2="0" .../> ... rotate each by 22.5 deg increments` Actually 8 spokes = 4 lines through center at 0,45,90,135 degrees gives 8 spokes. Add also 22.5 offsets for 16 spokes. Let's do 12 spokes: lines at 0,30,60,90,120,150 → but those give 12 spokes. Fine, 6 diameter lines.

I'll write explicit transform rotate.

Hub: small circle.

Tires: circle stroke width 12, dark. Rim: circle stroke 5 lighter.

Chain: two lines from chainring (r 26 at bottom bracket) to rear cog (r 12 at rear hub) plus chain ring circle.

Chainring circle at (390,420) r 26, teeth maybe. Rear cog r 14 at (250,420). Chain lines: top line from tangent (390,394) to (250,406); bottom (390,446) to (250,434). Approximate.

Crank arm: from (390,420) to (440,472) with pedal at (440,472). Other crank arm opposite: (390,420) to (340,368) with pedal there (draw behind, lighter).

Pedals: small rect rotated.

Feet: pelican feet webbed, orange. Foot on forward pedal at (440,470): draw webbed foot shape.

Legs: from body bottom (~360, 300) down to pedal. Draw leg as thick line stroke orange 10, with knee bend at (400,380)? Pelican legs are short-ish. Let's do leg path M 360 290 C 375 340, 420 420, 440 468.

Second leg (far side) at pedal (340,368): path M 350 290 C 345 330, 345 350, 340 366 — drawn behind body in darker shade. Draw before body.

Handlebar: head tube top at (500,326); bar goes up-left/right. For a pelican gripping, handlebar with grips at (520,318) and crossbar. Let's do handlebar as path: M 500 326 L 520 316 L 545 322 (grip). And a stem. Pelican wing tip reaches grip at (535,322).

Actually the pelican head at (470,190) is above handlebar; wing goes down-right to grip.

Hmm, the front wheel at (560,420) and handlebar around (520,316) — fork goes from (505,375) to (560,420). Fine.

Seat: at (320,310) — seat shape small triangle-ish path.

Let me reconsider pelican position relative to seat: seat at (322,308). Body center (340,262)? Body should sit above seat, body bottom ~ 300. Body ellipse rx 78 ry 58 center (350,258). Tail feathers at back-left (275,255).

Neck: from body top-right (400,220) curving up-right to head at (486,175). Neck thickness ~26. Draw as path with stroke width 26 round caps in body color, or as filled shape. I'll use a filled shape: path from (390,232) curving to (470,186) etc. Simpler: thick stroke.

Head: circle-ish at (486,178) r 26. Beak: long from head tip. Pelican beak points forward and slightly down. Upper mandible from (500,170) to tip (610,214); lower mandible/pouch from (492,196) curving down to (600,230) forming pouch. Let's craft:

Wing: shape over body: path from (300,230) to (410,235) sweeping down; wing tip extends to handlebar? Actually pelican uses wing as arm to hold handlebar. Draw wing: filled shape from shoulder (370,240) sweeping back-left to (285,250) then feather lines. Then a separate "arm" wing reaching forward to grip: from shoulder (400,240) curving to (528,318) tapering, ending at grip. That might look odd but reads well.

Better: draw the near wing as the arm reaching handlebar: shape from (380,235) to (520,305) narrow. And draw far wing as folded on the body silhouette behind (draw before body) with feather detail.

Hmm, pelicans have big wings; folding wing along body with feathers is nice; then a smaller visible arm going to the bar. I'll do: folded wing drawn on body (grey, feather strokes), plus the near wing extended forward-down to the handlebar grip — drawn as an elongated wing with feather tips.

Let me do near wing: path M 366 240 C 400 232, 460 260, 520 300 C 528 306, 526 316, 516 316 C 470 290, 410 262, 366 252 Z with feather lines. Fill #d8c6ad, stroke #b7a387.

Then grip at (520,306) — handlebar grip should be there. Adjust handlebar: head tube top (505,330); bar from (505,330) going right-up to (524,316) then grip to (546,326). Wing tip at (520,306) would be above grip. Let's place grip around (532,318) and wing tip overlapping at (524,312). Good enough visually — wing wraps over the grip. I'll add a small "foot/hand" at the grip.

Simplify: handlebar path: from stem top (505,332) up to (520,318), then bar to (556,326) with grip segment; draw grip as thicker rounded line from (528,320) to (556,328) in dark color. Wing tip covers around (520,312)-(540,322). OK.

Add helmet on head? A cute tiny helmet at top of head: path arc from (460,168) to (512,164) with strap. Might complicate. I'll add a small red cap/helmet — adds charm. Let's do a helmet: ellipse-ish path over head top: M 462 176 C 466 152, 500 148, 516 168 L 512 174 C 496 158, 474 160, 466 178 Z fill #2f6f6a. Plus strap line to cheek.

Hmm head center (486,178) r 26 → head top y≈152. Helmet covering top from y 148 to 176. Fine.

Scarf: around neck at (470,196) and trailing back behind: path from neck going back-left with wavy tails, red. Draw before body/neck? Scarf trailing should be behind neck but visible over sky. Draw scarf after neck, tails flowing left with two wavy strips. Nice motion.

Also add sunglasses? No, keep eye.

Extras: sun, clouds, road with dashes, motion speed lines behind rear wheel, small dust puffs.
